name: Forge 146 Fitness

hero.title: Show up.
hero.lead: Coached group classes for every level, from 5 AM to 7:30 PM. Your first class is free, and a coach walks you through it.
hero.imageAlt: A group class training with resistance bands under studio lights

trial.label: Start Your Free Trial
trial.title: Your first class is on us.
trial.text: Pick any class on the schedule, tell us you are coming, and a coach meets you at the door. No contract, no sales pitch.
trial.imageAlt: A row of heavy bags hanging in a dark gym

about.title: Forty-five minutes. A coach the whole time.
text: Every class at Forge 146 is planned by a coach and run by one, so the weights, the pace and the form get watched from the first rep to the last.
Beginners get scaled options and a little extra attention. Regulars get programming that moves forward week to week instead of repeating.
about.imageAlt: The training floor with racks and machines under low lights

classes.name: HIIT Burn
classes.summary: Short, hard intervals with ropes, bikes and bodyweight.
classes.text: Work and rest on a clock: forty seconds on, twenty off, around stations that change every round. You set the effort, and the coach keeps the pace honest.
expect: A ten-minute warm-up before the first interval
Stations for ropes, rowers, bikes and floor work
A scaled option for every movement
A cool-down and stretch to finish
classes.imageAlt: A woman working with battle ropes in the studio

classes.name: Strength Lab
classes.summary: Barbell lifts taught properly and loaded week by week.
classes.text: Squats, deadlifts, presses and pulls, coached in small groups so your form gets checked on every set. The program runs in six-week blocks, so the weight on the bar goes up on purpose.
expect: Technique work before the working sets
Your numbers written down and tracked
Accessory work for the back, hips and core
Groups capped at ten per coach
classes.imageAlt: A lifter setting up for a deadlift on a rubber floor

classes.name: Ride
classes.summary: Indoor cycling to a loud playlist and a coach who rides with you.
classes.text: Climbs, sprints and steady efforts on the bike, with the lights down and the music up. Low impact on the joints and hard on the lungs.
expect: A bike fitted to you before the first ride
Climbs, sprints and recovery rides
Clip-in or regular shoes, either works
Towels and water at every bike
classes.imageAlt: A row of indoor bikes in a dark studio

classes.name: Boxing Conditioning
classes.summary: Bag work, footwork and combinations, with no sparring.
classes.text: Learn the jab, the cross and the hook, then put them together on the heavy bag in timed rounds. Conditioning between rounds keeps the heart rate up.
expect: Wraps and gloves to borrow for your first class
Combinations taught from the stance up
Rounds on the heavy bag
No sparring and no contact
classes.imageAlt: A man training on a heavy bag

classes.name: Bootcamp
classes.summary: Tires, sleds and teams. The Saturday morning crowd favorite.
classes.text: A full-body session built on carries, pushes, pulls and partner work. Some days it is a circuit, some days it is a team challenge, every day it is coached.
expect: Partner and team workouts
Tire flips, sled pushes and carries
Scaled loads for every level
A different session every week
classes.imageAlt: Two people flipping a tire across the gym floor

classes.name: Mobility and Core
classes.summary: Slower work for hips, shoulders and trunk. The class that keeps you training.
classes.text: Controlled strength through full ranges of motion, kettlebell get-ups, carries and core work. Good on a recovery day and good for anyone who sits at a desk.
expect: Joint-by-joint mobility work
Kettlebell get-ups and carries
Core work without endless crunches
A pace anyone can follow
classes.imageAlt: A man doing a kettlebell get-up on the gym floor

classesIntro: Six class types, all coached and all scaled to your level. New here? HIIT Burn and Bootcamp are the easiest places to start.

membership.intro: No contracts and no sign-up fee. Freeze or cancel any time with a month's notice.

tiers.name: Drop-In
tiers.text: One class, any time on the schedule.

tiers.name: Unlimited
tiers.text: Every class, every week, as often as you want.
features: A goal session with a coach each quarter
Bring a friend free once a month

tiers.name: 8 Classes
tiers.text: Two classes a week, for a steady routine.
features: Book up to a week ahead

membership.note: Prices include tax. Student, first responder and military members get 15% off any monthly membership.

coaches.name: Marcus Bell
coaches.bio: Marcus runs HIIT Burn and Bootcamp and writes the conditioning program. He spent eight years coaching high school football before opening Forge 146.
coaches.imageAlt: Marcus Bell in a black tank top

coaches.name: Tasha Monroe
coaches.bio: Tasha coaches Strength Lab and Mobility and Core. She competes in powerlifting and loves teaching the first deadlift.
coaches.imageAlt: Tasha Monroe standing on the gym floor

coaches.name: Andre Silva
coaches.bio: Andre teaches Boxing Conditioning and leads the Ride classes. Expect loud music and a lot of encouragement.

coachesIntro: Every class is run by one of three coaches, and every one of them still trains on the same floor.

faq.q: I have never done a class like this. Can I keep up?
faq.a: Yes. Every movement has a scaled version, and the coach will show you which one to use. Plenty of members started with their first class here.
Training shoes, a water bottle and something you can move in. We have towels, and gloves and wraps for boxing.
Ten minutes before your first class, so a coach can show you around and set you up.

contactImageAlt: A squat rack and barbells on the training floor

reviews.author: Member since 2021
reviews.text: I was nervous walking into my first class and the coach checked on me the whole time. Two years later I still come four mornings a week.

reviews.author: Strength Lab regular
reviews.text: They actually teach you how to lift. My deadlift has gone up every block and my back has never felt better.

reviews.author: 5 AM crew
reviews.text: The early class is the best part of my day. Hard workout, good people, and I am still at my desk by eight.
